absent: Numeric addresses of machine check, APIC and threshold registers and numeric positions of status and control bits.
Allocation, initialization and teardown of per processor bank arrays, threshold lists, storm descriptors, timers and injection records.
Locking and lifetime rules for threshold bank lists and storm state beyond the observed interrupt suppression and discovery lock.
Contents and ordering of the Intel severity table and mapping of severity levels to system actions.
Behavior of pooled and direct logging channels, timer start primitives, and deferred message emission.
Feature detection and configuration of scalable MCA, systemic recovery, overflow recovery, succor and corrected interrupt support.
Threshold counting hardware semantics including overflow, count enable and interrupt type encodings.
Callers, scheduling context and error injection setup for polling, recheck and severity evaluation.

findings.text: Availability query indicates whether machine check handling may proceed for a processor description, reporting unavailable when globally disabled and otherwise requiring both exception and architecture capabilities.

Polling service examines machine check banks associated with the current processor and ensures each observed condition is assessed for storm relevance, classified for severity, recorded through a selected logging channel, and cleared, finishing with core synchronization while leaving global status untouched.

Non instrumentable register accessors provide reads and writes for machine check registers, transparently serving fault injection state when injection is active and otherwise performing hardware access with containment for architectural faults.

Address usability service reports whether an error address may be used for recovery, requiring address validity at the top level and applying vendor specific rules for legacy and scalable AMD designs and for Intel style granularity and mode checks, with conservative negative defaults when vendor support is not built in.

Severity service maps an error record with optional register context and exception indication to an action level, selecting AMD and Hygon evaluation versus Intel evaluation based on boot processor vendor.

Correctability predicate distinguishes errors that hardware has corrected or can tolerate from those requiring urgent action, treating deferred conditions on certain vendors and any uncorrected indication as not correctable.

Recheck entry re examines owned banks after a corrected interrupt, proceeding only when machine checks are available and corrected interrupt support is present, with interrupts suppressed across the poll.

Bank clearing service releases per bank status after logging, using an AMD specific path that also resets threshold state and handles deferred status separately, and a generic path that clears status, with a no operation fallback when AMD support is absent.

Storm management services track corrected error rates per bank, mark banks entering or leaving high rate mode, adjust notification thresholds in a vendor specific way, and start or relax periodic polling, with inert fallbacks when threshold support is not built in.
Interrupt service drain check observes all in service register state, acknowledges each asserted level when new assertions cannot appear, then re observes and reports whether the map is empty.
Polling and timer entries provide the invocation points for examining banks on demand, for re polling after corrected interrupts, and for switching periodic polling rate when storm mode changes.
No bank inspection occurs unless global disable is clear, required processor capabilities are present, and for the recheck path corrected interrupt support is confirmed.

When injection completion is signaled on the current processor, register accesses are satisfied from an injection record selected by bank specific mapping for reporting, status, address, misc and global status selectors, with unmapped selectors yielding zero on read and ignored on write.
Register number computation selects between scalable and legacy encodings based on processor capability, providing distinct numbers for control, address, misc and status selectors within each bank.

Record preparation always captures global status and, when register context is supplied, captures instruction location only when restart validity indications allow it, normalizes virtual mode code segment appearance, and prefers a dedicated reporting register for instruction location when configured.

Auxiliary capture reads only fields whose validity indications are set, applies granularity masking when systemic recovery is enabled, consults deferred registers when flagged, and on scalable systems additionally captures identification and syndrome state and refines the address using bank specific length encoding.

Poll logging favors valid correctable conditions and explicitly requested uncorrected scans, consults deferred status on scalable systems and marks deferred register use when appropriate, and otherwise suppresses uncorrected errors except for non enabled speculative cases and uncorrected no action required cases when systemic recovery is enabled.
Storm accounting observes every bank status before validity filtering so that absent errors contribute toward ending high rate mode, while banks flagged as poll only never participate in tracking.

AMD severity evaluation treats context corruption, overflow without recovery support, missing recovery support, and unrecoverable kernel context as fatal, deferred conditions as deferred, and correctable conditions as retainable, with context derived from privilege level, restart validity, and safe fixup or user copy evidence.

Intel severity evaluation selects the first table rule whose status, global status, recovery enablement, execution context, exception mode, processor model and stepping, and bank range all match, records coverage of the selected rule, and returns its associated action and message.

User copy detection inspects the faulting instruction for memory to register moves and repeated string moves, resolves the effective source, rejects kernel space sources, and records the user address for later handling when a user copy is recognized.

Threshold restart walks all blocks of a bank and reprograms each counting register to reset overflow and count or to adjust limits without reset, clears interrupt type selection, optionally updates locality offset when valid, enables interrupt delivery only when capable and requested, and always re enables counting.

Local vector offset changes are rejected on scalable systems, rejected when no vector was assigned, and rejected when the requested value differs from hardware programming, with firmware diagnostics emitted for the latter two cases.

End of interrupt signaling is issued once per asserted in service level with traversal order treated as irrelevant because no new levels can appear during the drain, and emptiness is determined by bitmap inspection before and after signaling.

Clearing on AMD resets threshold limits first, clears deferred status whenever a deferred indication was observed, and omits status clearing when deferred registers were used exclusively, while other vendors clear status directly.
Threshold updates serialize read modify write of the per bank control register under a dedicated discovery spin lock with interrupt state preserved across the critical section.

Recheck polling suppresses local interrupts across the entire bank scan, and threshold reprogramming tolerates concurrent offline transitions by abandoning work when per processor threshold state has disappeared except when updating locality offset.

Error record carries bank identifier, status, address, misc, global status, instruction location and segment, identification and syndrome values, severity, vendor identity, and kernel flags including deferred register use and recovery context markers.

Threshold state comprises per processor per bank lists of blocks each with register address, processor, bank and block numbers, limit, capability and enable flags, plus a restart carrier conveying target block, prior limit, and locality offset update request.

Storm descriptor holds per bank poll only indication, storm mode flag, last observation time, shiftable history of recent correctable results, and a per processor count of banks currently in storm mode.

A bank rests in normal mode until its recent correctable history reaches a begin threshold, then enters storm mode with vendor threshold adjustment, periodic polling, and poll list membership, and later returns to normal when recent history shows no correctable activity, restoring thresholds and relaxing polling.

Each polled bank moves from enabled and owned to skipped when control is clear or ownership is absent, to ignored when logging policy rejects the status, to recorded through pooled or direct channels, and finally to cleared, with global status never cleared in this path.

Threshold reprogramming selects among reset of count and overflow after interrupt or initialization, limit change without reset, and locality offset update, converging on a counting enabled register with interrupt delivery reflecting capability and enablement.
Interrupt drain starts in observed state, transitions to acknowledged once per asserted level, then to re observed, ending in empty success or non empty failure depending on final map state.
A fault while accessing machine check registers outside injection is treated as an architectural violation that halts further progress rather than returning partial data.

Context corruption, overflow without recovery support, and unrecoverable kernel execution are classified as fatal and must terminate processing, so misclassification risks silent corruption or unnecessary shutdown.

Concurrent reconfiguration against offline, and firmware supplied locality offsets that disagree with hardware, can leave threshold interrupts misdirected or disabled unless validation and abandonment rules are honored.
Machine check register selectors distinguish control, address, misc and status views per bank, with separate scalable and legacy numberings chosen by capability.

Status indications include valid, uncorrected, context corrupt, overflow, enabled, deferred, address valid, misc valid, syndrome valid, poison and physical address valid, while global status provides restart and instruction pointer validity used to judge recoverability.

Poll control flags request timestamp capture, pooled versus direct logging, and uncorrected inclusive scanning, while kernel flags record deferred register use and in kernel recovery eligibility including copy from user.
In service state is exposed as a fixed count of register words spaced at sixteen byte intervals and viewed as a bitmap of fixed width for emptiness and per level iteration.

Storm detection uses a bounded history width shifted by elapsed seconds, a begin population threshold, an end window over low history bits, and a one second periodic poll while any bank remains stormy.

Intel usability requires misc validity, address granularity not exceeding page shift, and physical address mode, while storm handling swaps per bank notification thresholds between a storm value and a stored normal value.
